item.title: [malware] Who is the Kimwolf Botmaster “Dort”?
item.description: In early January 2026, KrebsOnSecurity revealed how a security researcher disclosed a vulnerability that was used to assemble Kimwolf, the world's largest and most disruptive botnet. Since then, the person in control of Kimwolf -- who goes by the handle "Dort" -- has coordinated a barrage of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS), doxing and email flooding attacks against the researcher and this author, and more recently caused a SWAT team to be sent to the researcher's home. This post examines what is knowable about Dort based on public information.

item.title: [malware] ‘Starkiller’ Phishing Service Proxies Real Login Pages, MFA

item.title: [vulnerability] Google fixes Chrome zero-day with in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-5281)
item.description: <p>Google has fixed 21 vulnerabilities affecting its popular Chrome browser, among them a zero-day (CVE-2026-5281) with an in-the-wild exploit. About CVE-2026-5281 As per usual, information about the fixed zero-day is limited, and there&#8217;s no details about the exploit (or how/if it&#8217;s being used by attackers). CVE-2026-5281&#8217;s official description says it&#8217;s a use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability in Dawn, an open-source and cross-platform implementation of the WebGPU standard that&#8217;s used in Chromium and Chromium-based browsers. The vulnerability affects &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/google-chrome-zero-day-cve-2026-5281/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/google-chrome-zero-day-cve-2026-5281/">Google fixes Chrome zero-day with in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-5281)</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [threat-intel] Financial groups lay out a plan to fight AI identity attacks
item.description: <p>Generative AI tools have brought the cost of deepfake production low enough that criminals and state-sponsored actors now use them routinely against financial institutions. A joint paper from the American Bankers Association, the Better Identity Coalition, and the Financial Services Sector Coordinating Council lays out the scale of the problem and calls on federal and state policymakers to act across various areas. Deepfake incidents in the fintech sector increased 700% in 2023 compared to 2022. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/fight-ai-identity-fraud/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/fight-ai-identity-fraud/">Financial groups lay out a plan to fight AI identity attacks</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [malware] Malware detectors trained on one dataset often stumble on another
item.description: <p>Machine learning models built to catch malware on Windows systems are typically evaluated on data that closely resembles their training set. In practice, the malware arriving on enterprise endpoints looks different, comes from different sources, and in many cases has been deliberately obfuscated to evade detection. A study from researchers at the Polytechnic of Porto tests what happens when that gap is made explicit, and the results have direct implications for organizations relying on static &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/cross-dataset-malware-detection-research/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/01/cross-dataset-malware-detection-research/">Malware detectors trained on one dataset often stumble on another</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [vulnerability] Crypto industry may be running out of time to prepare for quantum attacks
item.description: <p>Google’s latest research suggests the cryptocurrency industry may have less time than expected to prepare for quantum computing. In a whitepaper, Google examines risks to elliptic curve cryptography, the system securing most blockchain networks. The researchers revisit earlier assumptions about how difficult it would be for a quantum computer to break these protections, concluding that the required resources may be lower than previously estimated. “To share this research responsibly, we engaged with the U.S. government &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/quantum-computers-cryptocurrency-risks-google-research/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/quantum-computers-cryptocurrency-risks-google-research/">Crypto industry may be running out of time to prepare for quantum attacks</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

[general] Apple’s Camera Indicator Lights
item.description: <p>A <a href="https://daringfireball.net/2026/03/apple_enclaves_neo_camera_indicator">thoughtful review</a> of Apple&#8217;s system to alert users that the camera is on. It&#8217;s really well-designed, and important in a world where malware could surreptitiously start recording.</p> <blockquote><p>The reason it&#8217;s tempting to think that a dedicated camera indicator light is more secure than an on-display indicator is the fact that hardware is generally more secure than software, because it&#8217;s harder to tamper with. With hardware, a dedicated hardware indicator light can be connected to the camera hardware such that if the camera is accessed, the light must turn on, with no way for software running on the device, no matter its privileges, to change that. With an indicator light that is rendered on the display, it&#8217;s not foolish to worry that malicious software, with sufficient privileges, could draw over the pixels on the display where the camera indicator is rendered, disguising that the camera is in use...</p></blockquote>

item.title: [general] As the US Midterms Approach, AI Is Going to Emerge as a Key Issue Concerning Voters
item.description: <p>In December, the Trump administration signed an executive order that <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/11/technology/ai-trump-executive-order.html">neutered</a> states&#8217; ability to regulate AI by ordering his administration to both sue and withhold funds from states that try to do so. This action pointedly supported <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/08/us/politics/trump-executive-order-ai-laws.html">industry lobbyists</a> keen to avoid any constraints and consequences on their deployment of AI, while undermining the efforts of consumers, advocates, and industry associations concerned about AI&#8217;s harms who have spent years pushing for state regulation.</p> <p>Trump&#8217;s actions have clarified the ideological alignments around AI within America&#8217;s electoral factions. They set down lines on a new playing field for the midterm elections, prompting members of his party, the opposition, and all of us to consider where we stand in the debate over how and where to let AI transform our lives...</p>
